title: W1 fix is inert: the review page's _focus_seconds field is hardcoded "0" and no JS ever populates it — focus_seconds_reported is still always 0 in a real browser
detail: The only writer of _focus_seconds is the per-question submit handler inside .ref-question sections on [data-testid='reference-form-page']. The review page (testid reference-review) has no such sections, so initBrowser early-returns and the field submits its hardcoded "0" — the exact r1 symptom W1 filed.
recommended_fix: In reference_form.js, attach a submit listener to [data-testid='reference-review-form'] that sets _focus_seconds from currentFocusSeconds(), persisting the accumulator across review navigation (e.g. sessionStorage); add a wiring test.

title: B1 fix leaves a dead https CTA for the localhost origin_domain (dev-only corner)
evidence:
form_handler.gleam:
      let origin = row.origin_domain
email_client.gleam:
  "https://" <> domain <> path

form_handler.gleam:694:
      base_url: domain_helpers.origin_from_domain(row.origin_domain),
detail: build_entity_url hardcodes https://; a dev vacancy's origin_domain is "localhost:4000" (validate_origin_domain), so terminal-notification CTAs become https://localhost:4000/... — dead against the local http server, while the invite email keeps http:// via origin_from_domain. Double-scheme gone; localhost CTA still dead.
recommended_fix: Special-case localhost/127.0.0.1 in build_entity_url to http:// (mirroring origin_from_domain), or strip the scheme from origin_from_domain's output before passing it.
